title: Signal Tiling — Priority currency for latency- and cost-sensitive roadmaps
creator: Aisha Khandelwal
description: Introduce a ‘Signal Tiling’ prioritization currency that converts product signals (user value, reach, confidence) together with operational costs (per-token cost, latency tail risk, SLA exposure) into a single, auditable score to drive cycle-level roadmap allocation. The intent is to produce a repeatable, explainable ranking that biases the backlog toward initiatives that maximize real product impact while keeping token economics and latency SLAs in bounds.
background: We currently have many RICE-like artifacts that focus on opportunity or latency separately. Engineering and infra teams report frequent late-cycle churn when high-value items cause unacceptable cost/latency regressions. Sales and CS ask for predictability (Dedicated/Private customers), while platform teams want a way to signal hard constraints. Signal Tiling is conceived to bridge product impact scoring with operational guardrails.
proposed_scoring: Score = (ImpactScore * Reach * Confidence) / Effort  - OpsPenalty. ImpactScore is a normalized customer-value metric (0-10). Reach is weekly active usage multiplier. Confidence is likelihood (0.0-1.0). Effort is story-points proxy. OpsPenalty aggregates two exponential penalties: CostPenalty = lambda_cost * max(0, (proj_avg_cost_per_token - baseline)/baseline)^2; LatencyPenalty = lambda_latency * P95_increase_ratio^1.5. Final score is scaled to a 0-100 priority currency.
example_calculation: Example: New caching rollout: ImpactScore=7, Reach=0.2, Confidence=0.8, Effort=8 -> base = (7*0.2*0.8)/8=0.14. Assume CostPenalty=0.03, LatencyPenalty=0.05 -> adjusted=0.14-0.08=0.06 -> scaled priority currency=6.0. Compare that to a smaller UX flow with base 0.09 and negligible ops penalty -> 9.0 after scaling; UX wins this cycle despite lower raw impact because ops cost and latency are low.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring formula documented in Confluence with worked examples
Priority currency computed for all candidate initiatives in Cycle 2025-W12
Stakeholder alignment (PM, Eng infra, SRE) sign-off on lambda_cost and lambda_latency
Top 20 backlog items re-ranked by currency and validated against historical decisions
A simple dashboard (Console) showing score components per initiative
decisions: Use effort in story points as denominator (aligned to PM/ENG convention)
Expose Cost and Latency penalties separately in UI so stakeholders can see trade-offs
Default lambdas: lambda_cost=12, lambda_latency=8 (to be tuned after two cycles)
Apply floor to Confidence at 0.2 to avoid under-weighting exploratory bets
open_questions: What is the canonical baseline for avg_cost_per_token? (hosted historical vs dedicated pricing)
How do we treat multi-quarter initiatives where latency regressions are addressed later in the same initiative?
Should regulatory or compliance work get a manual multiplier bypassing ops penalties?
implementation_notes: PMs will be given a Confluence template to fill ImpactScore / Reach / Confidence for each candidate
ENG to provide projected cost delta and P95 latency delta given proposed workload (ENG-18321 owner)
Small script in repo infra/roadmap/tools to compute currency from CSV input; proposed PR: github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap-tools/pull/142
Console team to add a score breakdown card (design spec link below) with hoverable tooltips
updates: 2025-03-02: Kickoff with Eng infra and SRE. Collected initial latency modeling templates (ENG-19002)
2025-03-04: PM guild reviewed scoring formula; requested explicit treatment for compliance work
2025-03-06: Prototype spreadsheet produced and applied to Cycle 2025-W08 backlog (results surprising: several high-impact infra items penalized heavily)
2025-03-09: Presented to GTM leadership; request to add customer-segment weighting for enterprise customers
qa_checklist: Unit tests for scoring script (edge cases: zero effort, zero confidence)
Integration test to import roadmap CSV and output ranked list
Manual review of top 10 ranked initiatives by PM and Eng lead
Visual smoke test for Console card rendering components
risks: Over-penalizing long-term platform work leading to technical debt
Gaming of input fields (inflated ImpactScore or deflated Effort)
Insufficient accuracy in cost/latency projections from infra models
Stakeholder pushback if transparency is low
